label: miso 85 dam outage
definition: (PROBE — REJECTED, superseded by 2026-07-24-miso-86-netrev-margin) MISO-native published outage overlay + net-revenue gas margin (determination NOT-YET). Two deltas on the 2026-07-20-miso-81-phantom-outage recipe: gas_offer_margin=true (the go-forward fuel-invariant $/MWh gas offer form, anchor 3.0492 $/MMBtu) and miso_native_outage_source=true - MISO's own published Multiday Operating Margin outage record (region x cause daily offline MW, UNPLANNED components) REPLACING the CAMPD unit-level outage derate. Full span 2023-2025, per-year chained, zero fitted scalars. The measured overlay is kept per rule 1 though it degrades the fit: its published grain carries no unit/fuel identity, so a uniform envelope hands coal back ~5 GW and derates a peaking fleet the per-unit record never says was out.
market_story: COAL_PRB +28.3 TWh / CC_REGULAR -22.7 TWh (2023) is NOT a market story - it is the measured overlay's grain showing through, and it is recorded as a MODEL MISS, not calibrated. MISO publishes generation outages only as a region x cause daily MW total (Multiday Operating Margin, OUTAGE sheet), with no unit or fuel identity, so the admissible transform is a UNIFORM availability envelope on the fossil-thermal fleet: 18.4% / 20.5% / 23.7% unavailable in 2023/24/25. The real fleet is nothing like uniform - the per-unit CAMPD record this replaces measures COAL 33%/33%/26% unavailable, ST_GAS 59%/53%/51%, CC_REGULAR 20%/21%/25%, CC_CHP ~8%, and CT 0% (peakers are outside the instrument's coverage entirely). MISO's coal fleet is old and carries far more outage than the fleet average, so a fleet-uniform rate returns ~5 GW of coal to the merit order that was actually out; being the cheapest steel in MISO it immediately displaces combined-cycle gas. The same uniformity takes ~4-5 GW off 22.4 GW of peakers that the per-unit record does not say were out, which is what manufactures the 2025 price tail (C3a +43.5%, 138 model hours >$200 vs 38 actual). What the published record DOES validate is the level and the timing: its unplanned unavailability (0.18-0.24) brackets the CAMPD stack's own (0.24), its Derated bucket peaks in July-August exactly as an ambient capability derate should, and its Planned bucket peaks at 36 GW in April - which is why Planned is excluded here (it is the model's own layer, and charging it to thermal is refuted by MISO's metered output on 12/15/61 days). The open root-cause issue is fuel attribution, not the record.
